:::{#thm-surprisal-log-half}
#### Surprisal as a logarithm to base one half

For a [value](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-realization) $x$ of a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) $X$
with $\P(X=x) > 0$,
the [surprisal](#def-surprisal) in [bits](#def-bit) is

$$s(x) = \log_{1/2} \P(X=x).$$

:::

::: {.proof}

Write $p = \P(X=x)$.
The [change of base formula](https://morrison-lab.github.io/mds/algebra-exponentials.html#rem-logarithm-formula) gives

$$\log_b y = \frac{\logf{y}}{\logf{b}}$$

for $y > 0$ and $b > 0$ with $b \ne 1$.
With $b = 1/2$ and $y = p$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
\log_{1/2} p
&= \frac{\logf{p}}{\logf{1/2}} \\
&= \frac{\logf{p}}{-\logf{2}} \\
&= -\frac{\logf{p}}{\logf{2}} \\
&= -\log_2 p \\
&= s(x).
\end{aligned}
$$

The step from the third to the fourth line is the change of base formula with $b = 2$.

:::
